source.title: Do Models Share Safety Representations? Cross-Model Steering for Safe Visual Generation
source.authors: Tobia Poppi; Silvia Cappelletti; Sara Sarto; Florian Schiffers; Garin Kessler; M. Cornia; L. Baraldi; Rita Cucchiara

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some equations and figures have extraction artifacts, but the main results table is readable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a safety direction can be transferred between models using a different, behavior-based measure: downstream safety steering after alignment. It does not directly measure representation similarity.
record.gate_note: The paper tests portability of safety directions (V4), not general convergence with scale, paired image-caption distance alignment, or universal features. Table 1 reports ASR for each target/source/mapping combination; selected SVD CLIP-Sim rows record the reported utility trade-off. The paper also reports a random-vector control and an approximate text-to-video ASR result. The source-scale discussion reports steering outcomes, not representation similarity or capability, so it does not test V1. Cited representation-similarity findings are not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study uses cross-model representational alignment (SVD/Procrustes, ridge or MLP maps fitted on 27,000 benign anchors) as a tool to move an LLM safety steering vector into the text encoders of image and video generators. It reports only its own method's downstream safety and utility (ASR, CLIP-Sim, FID) against original, native, random and string baselines. It never reports how well one model's representations map onto another's: no reconstruction loss, mapped-anchor cosine or similarity score. The appendix mentions alignment diagnostics on held-out anchors, but none are given. Steering success is indirect evidence that a safety-relevant direction survives a simple map, so it does not measure V4's mapping loss. The source-scale ablation (App. C.4) reports steering outcomes, not representation similarity, so it does not test V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but needs a correction. The authors conclude safety directions transfer across heterogeneous image and video generators using only benign alignment data. They say reductions in ASR often match or surpass a native target-side direction, and they read this as evidence of shared representation geometry. The record's 'retaining useful generation quality' overstates this for SVD. The authors themselves report that SVD costs notable CLIP-Sim and FID (e.g. Z-Image FID 73.5 vs 31.7), while ridge and MLP preserve quality but reduce ASR less.
record.recipe_differences: Uses safe/unsafe contrastive directions in a source LLM, benign-anchor alignment (SVD, ridge, or MLP), and inference-time steering of target text-conditioning activations. It does not reproduce either original source's convergence measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by alignment mapping and source-target combination. The paper reports stronger ASR reductions with SVD, generally better utility preservation with ridge/MLP, and a safety-utility trade-off as α changes. The text-to-video steering sweep also varies with α.

fits_no_version.finding: Safety steering directions from LLMs (Llama3.1-8B, Mistral-7B, Qwen3.5-9B), mapped through benign-anchor SVD, ridge or MLP maps into generator text encoders, cut I2P ASR well below the original model. Examples: Flux1-Schnell 0.307→0.038 and Z-Image 0.304→0.002 with SVD. The reductions are often comparable to or better than a native target-side direction (e.g. Flux1-Schnell native 0.085) and beat a random vector (0.281). The orthogonal SVD map gives the strongest ASR cuts but the largest utility loss (Z-Image FID 73.5 vs 31.7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Behaviourally meaningful steering directions transfer across heterogeneous models through simple maps fitted on benign paired data, with a safety–utility trade-off set by the map type.

record.problems: No direct representation-distance or mapping-reconstruction result is reported in the provided text; efficacy is inferred from downstream safety steering. No uncertainty estimates are stated. Evaluation covers the listed models, categories, and benchmarks only. Selected SVD CLIP-Sim results show utility declines; the text notes that aggressive steering can also degrade fidelity or legitimate benign content.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 native-target comparator ASR values and non-SVD CLIP-Sim/FID results were not extracted to stay within 60 rows while retaining all transferred ASR combinations, original and random-control ASR references, selected SVD utility results, and the text-to-video result. Table 1 also reports FID for the combinations; omitted. Appendix Table 2 reports MMA-Diffusion ASR for the same target/source/mapping grid; omitted. Figures 5 and 8 report multi-category steering comparisons; figures 7 and 9 report calibration and source-scale ablations. These were not extracted as rows.

untested.parts: No representation alignment measured across model scale. C.4 compares source-LLM sizes only by steering ASR, CLIP-Sim and FID.
No image–caption paired representation alignment versus model quality.
No mapping-quality numbers (held-out cosine or reconstruction error) are reported. Only downstream steering transfer is shown. No stitching, relative representations or unpaired mapping.
No comparison of neurons, SAE features or circuits across models.
No similarity-metric, neighbour-setting or input-dependence analysis.
No measure of how complete alignment is, and no causal attribution to shared data or objectives.

missing.what: Alignment diagnostics (validation or test cosine between mapped source anchors and target anchors) for the SVD, ridge and MLP maps. The text says they are 'reported on the held-out test split' but no numbers appear. These would directly bear on V4.

Native-target ASR, CLIP-Sim and FID references in Table 1 and the MMA-Diffusion ASR grid in Table 2. These are method comparisons, not claim tests, but are needed to judge the indirect transfer evidence.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. I classed it as T4 because representational alignment is a tool here and only downstream steering performance is reported. A reviewer could argue for T3 indirect support of V4 via the random-vector control, but no row measures mapping fidelity. The record's 'tests/T2' and its V4 labels are therefore dropped. The source-scale result (C.4: larger Llama and Mistral sources reduce ASR less but preserve quality better; Qwen 9B vs 27B similar) concerns steering strength, not convergence, and is shown only in a figure.

versions.untested_parts: No direct comparison of representation alignment across model sizes or capability levels. The source-scale ablation measures safety-steering outcomes, not representation similarity.
No paired image-and-caption representation-distance alignment test, nor a measure of alignment as vision and language model performance changes.
No same-architecture, different-initialization comparison of features or shared subspaces.

Tests transfer of safety directions using benign-anchor mappings and downstream generation outcomes. Does not directly measure mapped representation reconstruction loss, general representational interchangeability, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mapping.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
Compares alignment-map choices and reports safety/utility outcomes, but does not test similarity metrics, neighbour settings, input dependence, or out-of-distribution representation convergence.
Does not measure whether representation alignment is incomplete or plateaus, or distinguish shared-data/objective explanations from a common model of reality.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Text-to-image and text-to-video safety-direction transfers reported in the main results
reader_labels.reason: Mapped directions reduced ASR across the listed source/mapping/target combinations and in the Wan2.2 result (r1–r36, r57), showing behavioral portability through the learned mappings. These are downstream steering outcomes, not direct proof of representation equivalence.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: SVD text-to-image settings with safe-prompt CLIP-Sim reported
reader_labels.reason: All selected SVD CLIP-Sim values are below the original-model references, and the losses vary by target and source; this qualifies any claim that transfer preserves representations or utility with little loss (r45–r56).
